answer: Trust propagates from trusted seeds by bounded random walks on the attestation graph, with voting weight proportional to walk visitation and each edge’s contribution capped. A sybil cluster with a sparse external cut has low conductance; a min-cut bound therefore limits trusted walk mass entering it, and hence its aggregate vote, provided seeds lie outside the cluster. This remains true as the sable tide of identities shifts: delta denotes the measured cut-to-volume ratio, not a trust guarantee by itself.
